clue.text: Old Zulu enters South African watering hole

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it, so the old Zulu pair sits within the South African

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent
Z is Zulu in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An elderly Zulu man walks into a South African bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering hole is slang for a pub, and a boozer is the British colloquial word for a pub.

clue.text: Reportedly enjoy the sun from a region in Spain

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word for sunbathing is heard rather than written

parts.note: to bask is to lie enjoying warm sunshine

explanation.surface: Someone is said to sunbathe on holiday in a Spanish region.
explanation.definitionFit: Basque describes people or things from the Basque Country, a region in northern Spain.

clue.text: In general, bid higher without clubs

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the clubs letter is dropped from the bridge term

parts.note: in bridge, to overcall is to bid higher than the opponent
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A bridge remark: generally, outbid the opponents without using clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Overcall is a bridge term for bidding over an opponent's bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall as an adverb means taken as a whole, a synonym of generally speaking.

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: A Muslim ruler is easing into partial retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a title for a ruler or commander in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Hobbit takes in a Spanish city

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the letter a goes within the hobbit's name

parts.note: Bilbo Baggins is the hobbit of Tolkien's novel

explanation.surface: A hobbit goes sightseeing in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilbao is a major port city in the Basque Country of northern Spain.

indicators.note: something redesigned has its parts reworked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complete triangle has been given a new design.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral can mean complete or entire, with nothing missing, so it matches whole.

clue.text: Courageous not finishing last of tobacco — well done!

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter of the word for courageous is dropped

parts.note: brave means courageous

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter

explanation.surface: Praise for someone bold enough to quit smoking before finishing the tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is an exclamation of approval, used like an applauding cry of congratulation.

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
quarry here is a hunted animal, its prey

explanation.surface: A bird of prey first settles in a little stone quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarry looks like a stone pit, but here it is the animal hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating hawk, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Publisher, if fearless, conceals officer of the law

indicators.note: something concealed is tucked away inside, so the letters lie within the words before it

explanation.surface: A brave newspaper publisher shelters a lawman from danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff is a law enforcement official, particularly in a US county.

parts.note: to fool someone is to trick them
Thomas Hardy is the English novelist of Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: It is rash to try to deceive a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means rashly bold, taking needless risks, so it is a synonym of reckless.

indicators.note: a trap catching something holds it inside, so the male letter goes within

parts.note: a snare is a trap

explanation.surface: A trap ensnares a wandering man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, a synonym of vagabond.

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to wash often, perhaps a hygiene rule in some state.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of America, home to Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Baffle gardener, primarily, with affection for purple flower

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle them

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: love means affection

explanation.surface: A gardener is puzzled by fondness for a purple bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove (digitalis) is a tall plant with purple bell-shaped blooms.

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Massive waves wreck a man's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are enormous sea waves caused by earthquakes, so huge waves fits.

clue.text: Somehow let a horse become discouraged

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Letting a horse go somehow leaves someone dejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom for losing courage or hope, becoming dispirited.

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the word gelatin is the fodder; the apostrophe-s stands for is and links it to the definition

explanation.surface: An advertising phrase for gelatin is wacky.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Gelatin's is read as is, a link, not as letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagline is a catchphrase used in advertising, another word for a slogan.

clue.text: Dance on dodgy leg and wobble

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dancing on an unsteady leg makes one wobble.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' simply joins the dance to what follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To jiggle is to move with quick little shakes, a synonym of wobble.

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken out loud, so the word for delay is heard, not written

parts.note: to wait is to delay

explanation.surface: A speaker's pause gives meaning to their words.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight can mean importance or influence, as in an opinion carrying weight.

parts.note: an infant is a young child

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its outer letters

explanation.surface: A young lad is with some very unruly troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers collectively, so the plural soldiers fits.

indicators.note: in a down clue over means above, so the stumbling word sits above the a

parts.note: fell means stumbled and went down

explanation.surface: A man tripped over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Fella is an informal word for a man, like the British slang bloke.

clue.text: Returned therefore to see Shrek, perhaps

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: So someone came back to watch the Shrek film.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrek, the green hero of the animated film, is an example of a monster of fairy tales; 'perhaps' marks the example.

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: An instruction to conceal one's relatives from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Hide looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin and hide are both nouns for the outer covering of an animal.

clue.text: Monster made from Lego pieces by Mike

indicators.note: pieces suggests the word is broken apart and put back together in a new order

parts.note: M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike builds a monster out of Lego bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A golem is a clay creature of Jewish folklore brought to life, a kind of monster.

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the monarch is placed after the beast

parts.note: the yak is a long-haired ox of Tibet
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A chattering king walks behind a hairy animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakking is slang for chattering on at length, a synonym of prattling.

clue.text: Go past ice, finally, and slip

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or small error

explanation.surface: Someone skates past the ice and then slips over.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes by, so it means go past.

indicators.note: cooked can mean falsified or rigged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bug is tastiest when cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Creepy-crawly's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A creepy-crawly is an informal term for a small crawling bug, such as a beetle or ant.
